done_when: forge sync refreshes generated files while other items' work or land runs, and waits for or skips only what that run actually holds, saying so in one line

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The proof list covers a concurrent `forge work` run but omits the Done-when case of a concurrent `forge land` run. Its named test starts only `forge work`, so the list supplies no proof for land.
findings.title: Not done: proof list

findings.body: Raise: Test. The only new command-level test holds `forge work`; it never starts `forge land`. Land has a later close phase after `worker.work` returns (`src/forge/land.py:47-54`), so the current test would pass if sync failed during that normally reached phase. The Done-when item explicitly includes land.
findings.title: Not done: sync while forge land runs

findings.body: Raise: Test. The test creates one held item and checks the skip message, but creates no second item with an earlier-release chat to preserve. It would still pass if sync skipped every item's chat. The unlocked-item path is the migration under `with hold` at `src/forge/codex.py:335-351`, and the Done-when item requires skipping only what the run holds.
findings.title: Not done: only the held item's chat is skipped

findings.body: Raise: Test. Both parameterized cases call `_codex_repo_direct` with its default `client=False`. That helper writes `repo = "forge-source"` (`tests/test_codex_worker.py:114-132`); the `repo` fixture also starts as a plain Git repo (`tests/conftest.py:312-324`). Thus neither case exercises a newly initialized client or an earlier-release adopted client as the proof list claims. The repository's review rule requires both client paths for a Forge change.
findings.title: Not done: concurrent sync in new and adopted client repos

why: forge sync refuses whenever any other item's forge work or land is running on the machine, so workers copy the guide by hand
